title: New Jersey AI Laws

reading.body:
New Jersey has enacted one AI-related law, and it targets algorithmic rent-setting rather than AI development, deployment, or data centers.

The law is A3497, the Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent Act, passed July 20, 2026. It makes it unlawful under the New Jersey Antitrust Act for rental property owners to use coordinators that perform coordinating functions, for coordinators to facilitate agreements among owners that restrict competition, for two or more persons to engage in parallel pricing coordination, and for any person to perform a coordinating function. It defines algorithmic device, coordinating function, and competitively sensitive information, and it requires the Attorney General to establish a complaint location and authorizes rulemaking.

The pattern is narrow. This is antitrust enforcement aimed at software that lets landlords price in parallel, not a framework governing how AI systems are built or trained. For AI specifically, the relevance runs through compute only indirectly: the law constrains a class of algorithmic coordination, and says nothing about the buildings, power, or chips that make such systems run.

What this does not tell the reader is how the law will be enforced, what penalties attach, or whether other states have copied it. It also does not cover any New Jersey law on data centers, grid interconnection, or AI procurement, because the data contains only this one enacted law.

Enacted AI laws in New Jersey

1 law this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • A3497: Establishes "Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act." passed 2026-07-20

    The act makes it unlawful and a violation of the New Jersey Antitrust Act for rental property owners to use coordinators that perform coordinating functions, for coordinators to facilitate agreements among rental property owners that restrict competition, for two or more persons to engage in parallel pricing coordination, and for any person to perform a coordinating function. It defines key terms such as algorithmic device, coordinating function, and competitively sensitive information. It requires the Attorney General to establish a complaint location and authorizes rulemaking.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for New Jersey. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
